findings.title: Events between index build and watch start are dropped
findings.body: `init` builds each index from storage (`s.build` on line 190) but discards the per-resource resource version returned by `s.build`, then starts `WatchWriteEvents` only after all builds complete (line 203). The SQL backend's `WatchWriteEvents` starts from the latest RV at the time it is called. Any write that commits after the list query for a resource but before this watch start is neither included in the built index nor delivered on the new watch channel, leaving the search index permanently stale for that event until a full rebuild. This is especially likely now that init runs as a blocking startup step while other instances may write.

findings.title: Search watch goroutine can panic on closed event channel
findings.body: The watch goroutine receives with `v := <-events` without checking whether the channel is closed. The SQL backend poller closes its event channel when it exits on Stop, so this loop will receive a nil `*WrittenEvent` and call `s.handleEvent(watchctx, v)`, which dereferences `evt.Type` and panics. The goroutine also uses `context.Background()` rather than a cancellable context, so it cannot be stopped by server shutdown. Because `NewResourceServer` now eagerly calls `s.Init`, this goroutine is always started. Use the server/backend context for cancellation and check `v, ok := <-events`.

findings.title: Data race in concurrent index build goroutines
findings.body: The worker goroutines started by `errgroup` concurrently write shared variables: `totalBatchesIndexed++` on line 189 and `_, _, err = s.build(...)` on line 190, where `err` is the outer function variable. These unsynchronized writes race under the Go race detector, can lose increments for the span event count, and make the code's behavior undefined. Use a local error variable inside each closure and update the counter safely (or compute it after `Wait`).

findings.title: Lock change allows duplicate concurrent builds for the same index key
findings.body: `BuildIndex` no longer holds `cacheMu` for the whole build, only when inserting into the cache. However, `searchSupport.getOrCreateIndex` still performs a non-atomic `GetIndex` then `build`. Two callers for the same missing key can therefore enter `BuildIndex` concurrently. For file-backed indexes both can call `bleve.New` on the same directory and build the same index, causing open/create contention; the loser remains open/leaked and whichever finishes last wins the cache. Distinct keys can be built in parallel, but same-key builds need a per-key lock or singleflight.
